title: Moore graph of degree 57 (srg(3250, 57, 0, 1))
statement: Find a 57-regular graph on 3250 vertices with diameter 2, equivalently a strongly regular graph srg(3250, 57, 0, 1) (girth 5, every two non-adjacent vertices with exactly one common neighbour). Hoffman and Singleton (1960) showed that a Moore graph of diameter 2 has degree 2, 3, 7 or 57; the first three exist and degree 57 is open. A valid graph scores 1.
submission: Text file: the graph in graph6 or sparse6 (as on House of Graphs), as an edge list (one edge "u v" per line, vertices numbered from 0) or as a 0/1 adjacency matrix.
score: 1 for a valid graph; none is known, so the best known value is 0

best_known.source: no Moore graph of degree 57 is known: Hoffman and Singleton (1960); F. Comellas's degree-diameter table states that Moore graphs of diameter 2 exist for degree 3 and 7 and '(perhaps) 57'; read 9 Nov 2026

provenance.keeper: F. Comellas, The (Degree, Diameter) Problem for Graphs
